title: Week 45: the case of the silent API
intro: This week we chased a login page that spun forever, rethought where caching lives, and wrote a launch email that went to the wrong timezone. Three units, one per lesson.

units.concept: Check the address before the code
units.story: The login spinner never stops. No error in the console, nothing in the server logs. We spent two hours reading auth code. The bug was one number.

items.q: The frontend calls the API and waits forever. The server log shows no request at all. Where do you look first?
opts: The URL and port the frontend calls
items.why: No request in the server log means the request never reached this server. Start with where it is sent, not what the server does with it.

items.q: The API listens on 8080 but the frontend config says API_URL=http://localhost:___ . We found 3000. What should it be?
items.why: A mismatched port fails silently when the other port has nothing listening, or worse, when another app answers.

items.q: Put the debugging steps in the order that would have saved us two hours.
steps: Check the request leaves the browser
Check it arrives at the server
Only then read the handler code
items.why: Follow the request from outside in. Each step halves where the bug can be.

items.q: Write a one-line check that prints OPEN if something listens on the port, else CLOSED. Port 9 is almost always closed.
items.why: A ten-second port probe beats an hour of reading code.

units.concept: Caches go where the data changes least
units.story: On the whiteboard, caching every API response looked clean. In practice, user profiles changed every few seconds and people saw stale names.

items.q: Which data is the safest to cache for an hour?
items.why: Cache what rarely changes. Country codes change once a decade; a cart changes every click.

items.q: In two sentences: why did the design look right on paper but fail in practice?
rubric: Names that the data changes faster than the cache expires
Says the change rate was only visible with real usage
items.model: The diagram treated all responses alike, but profile data changed faster than the cache lived. We only saw the change rate once real users edited their profiles.

units.story: Not code this time: the launch email said 'live at 9:00'. Half the readers were six hours away.

items.why: A time without a zone is a guess. Give the zone, and the reader's local time when you know it.
